Description: Supplication to papal curia concerning Josquin’s rectorate at St-Aubin, in the diocese of Bourges (12 km south of Issoudun): “Judocus de Pres, rector parochialis ecclesie sancti Albini Bituricensis diocesis ... devote creature vestre .N. sancte Romane ecclesie cardinalis vulgariter nuncupatus familaris continuus commensalis”. (The odd “N” means that no cardinal had been named.) He requests permission to hold the benefice for five years without residence and without being ordained priest—which is a major privilege for those who are not papal employees, so nobody need be surprised if it was not granted.

Archbishop of Aix signs letter of collation for “Jusquinus de Pratis”, singer and chaplain to René of Anjou, to a chaplaincy in Puy-St-Reparade, and permutated from the church of Ste Marie Madeleine also within the archbishop’s collation. Would seem to provide support for concluding that Josquin was in René's chapel already by 1475.
René of Anjou grants expectative to “Jossequin des prez chantre” of prebend at the collegiate church of St Maxe in his castle at Bar-le-Duc; Josquin is not mentioned as being present.
Josquin has obligation to Sebastianus de Ursis, priest of the diocese of Aix-en-Provence

Letter of collation from Georges-Olivier de Pannard, Archbishop of Aix, giving a chaplaincy at Aix Cathedral to “Jusquinus de Pratis”, singer and chaplain of René, after resignation of a benefice at a parish church in the diocese of Anjou. The writing of the year is hard to decipher, but more likely to be 1478, when 19 May was a Tuesday, whereas in 1476 it was a Sunday.

“Jacobus despres rector parochialis ecclesie Sancti Albini Bituricensis diocesis Ascanii Marie ... capellanus et familiaris continuus commensalis”, requests and is granted dispensation to hold the benefice for three years without being ordained priest. Surrounding documents make it clear that “Jacobus” is a slip of the pen.
Supplication of “Judocus de Pratis, clericus Cameracensis diocesis” for privileges given in the next document.

Papal letter (in response to the preceding) granting Josquin benefice facilities, including that of non-residence, and that of holding three incompatible minor benefices in the dioceses of Liège, Cambrai, Tournai and Thérouanne, even in an area with a language other than his own.

Papal letter to “Judoco de Pratis . . . continuus commensalis noster [standard langauage for a member of the papal household] et in Capella nostra cantor capellanus” [a singer-chaplain] grants him canonry and prebend at St-Omer. The effect of the bull is backdated to 1 November 1486; Starr writes (p. 47) that this "was simply the offical date used in the conferral of expectatives during the reign of Innocent VIII. The clause was used in cases where the petitioner submitted a request for  an expectative benefice after the date when they were "officially" conferred. Each of these documents from 1489 suggests the normal behavior of a newly employed papal familiar anxious to begin the acquisition of benefices." This papal letter reserves Josquin a benefice in the collation of the Abbey of St-Ghislain in the diocese of Cambrai, with the commissioners named as the Bishop of Tournai (Jean Montissart) and Nicolaus Rombert (canon of Cambrai). There seems no evidence of Josquin having actually received the St-Omer canonry or anything from St-Ghislain.

Papal record of obligation of “d. Judocus de Pratis, clericus Cameracensis diocesis, in capella sacri palatii cantor” to pay taxes on resigning and permutating “omnia beneficia ecclesiastica que obtinet” from the bull of 18 Aug 1489.

“Jodocus de Pratis” tries to eject Stephanus le Fevre from parish churches of Moustiers (this must be the modern Moustier lez Frasnes, 18 km east of Tournai) and St Michel de St-Sauveur et Dergneau (evidently the St-Sauveur 6 km north of Moustier lez Frasnes), both in the diocese of Cambrai, on the grounds of his not having the right dispensations.47 Given that Marbrianus de Orto submitted a similar supplication on 13 July (I-Rasv Registra Supplicationum 979, f. 19v), Sherr guesses that there was a lawsuit involving Josquin, Orto and Le Fevre during these years. Sherr: Josquin asks for more time to publish bulls regarding two parish churches in the diocese of Cambrai. He says that he had recently claimed the parish churches of Monstiers and of St. Michael de St. Sauveur et Deigman in the diocese of Cambrai, that had been held for a number oi years by Stephanus Le Feure (meaning that he wished to supplant Le Feure). Chancery regulations required in this case (an attempt to deprive someone of a benefice) that the present possessor be called before the judges within six months of the claim, and that the final sentence be delivered within a year.' Josquin says that he had received a decision in his favor and had published the bulls regarding the church of Monstiers, but had not been able to publish the bulls concerning the other church within the required time period. He therefore asks for a prorogation of another year to publish those bulls. This means that the original action had been initiated at least a year and probably a year and a half before the date of this supplication, in 1491 or 1492. In fact, Josquin was not the only papal singer who sought these benefices. In a supplication dated 13 July 1493 (that is, before Josquin's request for a prorogation), Marbrianus de Orto also asked for these churches, stating specifically in his supplication that Le Feure was to be deprived of them because he had not received a dispensation allowing him to hold incompatible benefice. Two weeks later, Le Feure himself submitted a supplication specifically asking for the dispensation. lo We may infer from all of this that there was a lawsuit involving Josquin, De Orto, and Le Feure in the years ca. 1491–93, the records of which have yet to be found.

Papal letter (from Corneta) to deans of Condé and Soignies and to Johannes de Porta, canon of Cambrai, to investigate Josquin’s (“Indocus [sic] de Pratis”) accusation that Emericus de Honstat obtained his chaplaincy at Bas-Ittre (now Ittre, 7 km northwest of Nivelles) in the diocese of Cambrai by means of a simoniacal arrangement with his predecessor, Martinus Kegels.

Papal letter to deans of Cambrai (Gilles Nettelet) and Nivelles (perhaps Marbrianus de Orto) and the Official of the diocese of Cambrai, instructing them to proceed with the induction of “Indocus [sic] de Pratis” to a canonry and prebend at St Géry, Cambrai, vacated by the death of Nicolaus Menent. There is no evidence that Josquin ever actually became a canon of St Géry.
